- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is trending upward, model frequently underestimates the continuation; add 1–2% to forecast for momentum bias.
- Model tends to lag in early days of a new trend (e.g., after a 10+ day downtrend); forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% for the first 3–5 days of reversal.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model often averages out extremes; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: higher sentiment → higher forecast, lower → lower, with decay factor of 0.8 per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period price spikes (last 7–10 days); increase forecast by 1–3% for final 7 days if sentiment is rising or neutral.
